### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 488f4f546556527d03e9afe92b7ffe466f342a2a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a0ecbd928b130a0e8bbc37c7182a5176e37f6107` — the merge of head `3283cefddb24bd488852da82efc9287828407421` into base `488f4f546556527d03e9afe92b7ffe466f342a2a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a0ecbd928b130a0e8bbc37c7182a5176e37f6107 && git checkout a0ecbd928b130a0e8bbc37c7182a5176e37f6107
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 488f4f546556527d03e9afe92b7ffe466f342a2a 3283cefddb24bd488852da82efc9287828407421 && git checkout -B drift-repro 488f4f546556527d03e9afe92b7ffe466f342a2a && git merge --no-ff 3283cefddb24bd488852da82efc9287828407421

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 488f4f546556527d03e9afe92b7ffe466f342a2a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## ACCEPT — `patch` confirmed, and the premise that moved is measured

Head judged: `3283cefddb24bd488852da82efc9287828407421`, merge-base `f9e16d856b`. Read at 2026-09-20T20:15Z.

### ⭐ The one claim the whole changeset level hangs on, verified with a lit control

If this diff moved the exit code off `0`, a script that succeeds today would start failing — a narrowing of a published CLI accept set, which ships `minor` + `**BREAKING**` + ADR-0087, ⛔ never `patch`. So the `patch` verdict rests entirely on the exit code not moving, and that is the one thing worth proving rather than reading:

| probe | reading |
| --- | --- |
| `this.exit` / `process.exit` added or removed **in the diff** | **0** |
| ⭐ control — the same probe over the whole file, **both refs** | `2` → `2` (the `catch` arm's two, untouched) |

The control is non-zero on both sides, so the diff's zero is a reading and not a broken probe.

⚠️ **My first run of this check was vacuous and I nearly published it.** `git fetch origin main <branch>` leaves `FETCH_HEAD` pointing at the *first* ref, so `git diff $(merge-base) FETCH_HEAD` was **main against main** — an empty diff whose "0 hits" meant nothing, and whose `2 → 2` control looked perfectly healthy because both sides were the same tree. Caught only because `merge-base == branch` was printed beside it. ⇒ ⛔ print the two shas a diff is actually between, every time; a control cannot detect a probe that is comparing a ref with itself.

### The remedy, read in the source

`if (result.success === false)` → `printWarning(...)`, else today's sentence. Three things about it are right in ways the order did not ask for:

- **`=== false`, not falsiness**, with the reason stated where a later reader will meet it: `false` is the protocol's positive *"no row was deleted"*, while an absent or `undefined` flag from an off-contract server is **not a signal at all** — and turning "no signal" into "not deleted" would make this command deny deletions that really happened. That matches `MetadataProtocol.deleteData`'s own reading of the driver contract.
- **`printWarning`, not `printError`** — the command completed; the server declined. Those are different facts and the CLI has a carrier for each.
- **The exit-code reasoning is written into the code, not just the PR.** Moving only the human arm off `0` would re-create *this very card's defect one layer down* — the same call exiting `0` under `--format json` and non-zero by default. That is the sharpest sentence in the round, and it is the argument that settles the level.

### Pins

All four the order required, plus two controls it did not ask for:

- `POSITIVE CONTROL — a success: false body reaches the command through the REAL SDK` ⭐ the anti-impostor control: it proves the seam under test is the real one, not a mock that would pass whatever the code did.
- `LIT CONTROL — success: true still prints today's sentence, byte for byte`
- `success: false — the human arm does NOT assert a deletion`
- `all three arms state the SAME fact, for one and the same result`
- `the exit code is 0 on BOTH arms and all three formats`
- `a genuine transport failure still exits 1 — the not-deleted arm did not swallow the error path`

The ablation is the right shape too: mutating `if (result.success === false)` → `if (false)` turned **exactly two** red — the not-deleted pin and the three-arms-agree pin — while the lit control and both exit-code pins stayed green, so it did not simply break everything. Restore proven by blob identity (`160538b32cd2` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty), ⛔ not by an editor's exit code.

### ⚠️ A premise moved under this round, and the dev caught it

The dispatch order and the card both record **PR #19411 as open and still a draft**, and conclude the contradiction is therefore *latent*. **It is not latent any more.** Verified independently on `origin/main`:

- `f9e16d856b` — *"fix(security,metadata-protocol): a packaged permission set's DELETE stops reporting a deletion it did not perform (#19411)"* — is on `main`.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:11465` now reads `success: deleted !== 0`, against a lit control on `deleteData` in that package.
- This PR's own merge-base **is** `f9e16d856b`, so it is built on the tree where the contradiction is live.

⇒ the fix is no longer pre-emptive; it closes a contradiction that a user can hit today. Nothing about the remedy changes — but the record should not keep saying "latent", so it is corrected here.

### Docs sweep — done, clean negative, and it cost two impostor controls

The drift check derived **2 anchors** and listed **0 pages**, stating in its own words that this is *"not a clean bill of health"*. This diff changes a user-visible CLI sentence, which is exactly the class the check structurally cannot see (a page quotes the **output**; the check anchors on the **emitter**). So it was swept by hand on `origin/main` `488f4f5465`:

- **`Record deleted:` → 0 files** in `content/docs`. No page documents `os data delete` at all.
- ⭐ **Lit control, found only on the third attempt:** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:597` quotes `✓ Build complete (74ms)` verbatim — glyph included — from `printSuccess` at `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts:1008`; and `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx:73` quotes `✓ Environment created!` from `environments/create.ts:141`. ⇒ this corpus **does** transcribe CLI success lines, so the zero above is an absence the instrument could have seen.

⛔ **The two impostors, recorded because counting hits would have given a wrong green twice:**

1. `Record created` → 1 hit, which looked like the sibling `printSuccess` sentence. It is `releases/v17/17-0.mdx:1553`, a **Studio flow-node trigger name** (*"Record created or updated"*). Unrelated.
2. `data delete` → 1 hit, which looked like the command. It is `references/api/protocol.mdx:730`, a **metadata-delete protocol** `success` field row. Unrelated.

Both were satisfied by a mechanism other than the one under test, and both were detectable only by opening the hit. ⇒ **no page is falsified by this change; nothing to file.**

### Level and gates

`'@objectstack/cli': patch`, `Clause-②: no`. `skip-changeset` refused by the dev's measurement from the artefact side (the new sentence reaches `dist/commands/data/delete.js`, with the unchanged `Record deleted` sentence from the same file as the lit control and the new test file absent from `dist` as the negative control). Not `minor` + BREAKING, because — per the verification at the top — no published accept set moves.

File surface is exactly the order's fence: `delete.ts` + one new sibling test + a changeset. No fourth file.

Readying and arming auto-merge.
